checks.detail:
AC-3 is not_met (The mechanism works when a PR title starts with the ticket ID.
- Real Linear plus real GitHub for the TRU-10 branch: the TRU-10 card showed Build round 1 pass, read from .sdlc/records/TRU-10/build-1.json on feat/tru-10-prs-gates-needs-you. The PR showed as checks pending; 3b60d49 has 0 check runs.
- The TRU-8 card got Plan round 2 pass from its real Linear comments, so the comments query works against real Linear.
- With the titles rewritten to start with the ID, booking's TRU-6/TRU-7 cards showed 'Adversarial review round 1: pass' from the real record files, and 'PR #49 checks pass' / 'PR #53 checks pass' from the real check-runs.
The gap: the real pipeline PRs in bbooth/booking name their ticket at the end, e.g. #49 'Drop Tenant.display_name and Tenant.coach_mode from the API (TRU-6)' and #53 '... (TRU-7)'. With those real titles served as open, the GitHub source returned prs=2 (sdlc-board only), and both booking PRs were silently dropped. A booking sub-ticket with an open pipeline PR would show no PR and no branch gate. The ticket's own e2e ('against bbooth/booking, a merged pipeline PR and TRU-6's records show on its card') fails on real data. The plugin's PR gate (check-pr.mjs names_ticket) accepts the ID anywhere in the title or body, so a prefix is not a pipeline convention.)

crates/server/src/main.rs:471 and docs/STATUS.md say GITHUB_TOKEN is optional for public repos. Without a token, each 60 s refresh makes at least 1 request per repo plus 3 per ticket PR (pulls, check-runs, records dir, record file). With the two configured repos and no PRs that is about 120 requests an hour, over GitHub's unauthenticated limit of 60, so the GitHub source goes stale within about 30 minutes.

crates/server/src/github.rs:390 checks() reads only check-runs: commit statuses (the /status API) are ignored, and a PR with no check runs is 'pending' forever. Observed: sdlc-board 3b60d49 has 0 check runs and shows checks pending, so a repo without Actions CI never gets a 'merge' item in Needs you.
crates/server/src/board.rs:217 prs.iter().find picks the first PR whose title names the ticket. A ticket with two open PRs, or the same ID in two repos that share the TRU key, shows one arbitrary PR.
